text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- November unemployment reaches 12.7 percent, breaking previous record.
-- OFCE economic institute says France's 1997 national budget will trim 0.2 percent off GDP growth.
-- First figures show 1.6 percent rise in 1996 petrol consumption over 1995.
-- Truck makers Renault VI and Sisu Oy finalise parts, cabin-making and distribution pact.
-- Societe Generale drops Peugeot from its European portfolio, and brings in Rhone Poulenc.
-- Government reserves right to sell less than 10 percent of France Telecom in April 15-30 timeframe, but maintains statutory right to majority stake.
-- Moody's lifts Credit Agricole unit Banque Indosuez long-term bank deposits to Aa2 from Aa3.
-- Finance ministry to pay out 15 billion francs in bonuses on PEP home savings and loan schemes in 1997.
-- GAN refused to comment on a report it would ask for up to 10 billion francs of French government aid.
